full_judgment:
2. The petitioner was a candidate in the election for the office of Chairman, Nabinagar Upazila Parishad, District Brahmanbaria held on 16.3.90. He along with six others including the respondent No. 5 contested the said election. The petitioner alleges that by notification dated 4.11.89 two unions namely, East Sadekpur and West Sadekpur (Barail) were taken out of Nabinagar Upazila and annexed to Brahmanbaria Sadar Upazila (Annexure 'A'); that on 15.2.90 Electoral Roll was finally published showing the said two unions under Nabinagar Upazila (Annexure 'D'); that on 22.2.90 the Deputy Com- missioner directed Upazila Nirbahi Officer to take action in pursuance of aforesaid notification dated 4.11.89 (Annexure 'C'); that on 1.3.90 Election Commission published a notification fixing 16.3.90 for holding election of Chairman, Nabinagar Upazila; that the petitioner and his large number of supporters amongst the voters of the said two unions were seriously prejudiced by the taking away of the said two unions from Nabinagar Upazila just before the election not for public interest; that the petitioner has all along love and support from voters of the said two unions; that the respondent No.5 who was below 25 years of age on the date of filing nomination paper on 17.2.90 as appears from the voters list (Annexure 'E') filed the nomination paper for the office of Chairman on that date; that objection raised about disqualification of the respondent No.5 was overlooked by the Returning Officer; that the petitioner and voters of the said two unions could not know about taking away of the said two unions from Nabinagar till two days before the date of election and as a result the voters boycotted the election; that the petitioner deployed all his resources for mobilization of support of the voters of the said two unions contiguous to his own union having largest number of supporters there but due to illegal and malafide action of the authority he lost their votes in the said election; that in the said election the petitioner secured 31,097 votes, respondent No. 5 secured 35,718 votes (Annexure F) and the respondent No.5 was declared elected Chairman by the Returning Officer; that the respondent No.5 being disqualified was illegally declared elected and his name was illegally published in the official Gazette on 31.3.90 (Annexure G). 

 3. The respondent No. 5 controverted the allegations made in the petition by filing a counter-affidavit denying material allegations and stating, inter alia, that the said two unions being contiguous to Brahmanbaria Sadar Upazila and having better communication facilities with Brahmanbaria Sadar Upazila than with Nabinagar Upazila and for administrative convenience with spontaneous public support were taken away from Nabinagar Upazila and added to Brahmanbaria Sadar Upazila for greater interest of the people; that in the voters list published on 5.8.83 the age of respondent No.5 was 21 years and date of birth of respondent No. 5 as per SSC Examination Certificate is 1.11.1960, (Annexure-A and A1 to the affidavit-in-opposition); that question of disqualification of respondent No. 5 was raised by Abdul Latif, Advocate in Writ Petition No. 650 of 1990 and the said petition was rejected on 10.4.90; that the respondent No.5 along with his nomination paper filed an application stating that due to printing mistake in the voters list published on 15.2.90 his actual age was not shown and relying on the SSC Examination Certificate and voters list of 1983 the Returning Officer found the age of respondent No. 5 to be about 29 years and accepted his nomination pa- per without any objection from other contesting candidates (Annexure 'A' 2 to the affidavit-in-opposition); that the petitioner was quite aware of the taking away of the said two unions from Nabinagar Upazila from long before the election and the voters of the said two unions did not boycott the election but they spontaneously took part in the election; that the petitioner has filed Election Tribunal Case No. 3 of 1990 in the Court of Election Tribunal, Brahmanbaria challenging the election of the respondent No. 5 (Annexure 'B' to the affidavit- in-opposition); that the petitioner having earlier filed a case in the Election Tribunal his writ petition is not maintainable; that the petitioner secured 3rd position and Abdul Latif (Advocate) secured 2nd position in the said election; that Abdul Latif (Advocate) filed Writ Petition No. 650 of 1990 and the same was rejected; that the petitioner having filed this writ petition suppressing the fact of his filing the casein the Election Tribunal on the same grounds, the present writ petition filed by him is not maintainable in law as decided by their Lordships of the Appellate Division reported in 40 DLR (AD) 270. 

 5. Mr. Md. Fazlul Karim, the learned advocate for the petitioner, submitted, referring to section 7 of Electoral Rolls Ordinance 1982, section 8 of Local Government Ordinance 1982, rule 4 of Upazila Parishad (Election of Chairman) Rules 1983, that the petitioner as well as the voters of the said two unions have been seriously prejudiced by publishing the names of those voters within the electoral area of Nabinagar Upazila and actually not allowing them to vote in the election for Chairman of Nabinagar Upazila. In support of his contention the learned Advocate relied on the case of Chief Commissioner of Ajmeer Vs. Radheshyatn Dhani reported in AIR 1957 (SC) 304. He further submitted that the respondent No. 5 was of the age of 23 years on the date of final publication of voters list on 15.2.1990 and as such he was below 25 years of age on the date of filing nomination paper on 17.2.90 and as such he was disqualified under section 6(1)(b) of the said Ordinance. He further submitted that voters list was published under rule 18 of the Election Rolls Rules and under section 17 of the Electoral Rolls Ordinance 1982 validity of the electoral rolls cannot be challenged before any Court and the Returning Officer is bound by the entry in the electoral rolls and he acted illegally in accepting the nomination paper of the respondent No. 5 who was disqualified to contest the election and in deciding the question of age of the respondent No. 5. He relied on the decision in the case of Munshi Abdul Hoque Vs. Additional Deputy Commissioner reported in 17 DLR 744 in support of his contention. He further submitted that his client had withdrawn the case filed before the Election Tribunal on 20.5.90 as the Tribunal was not competent to decide the questions of delimitation of area of the Upazila and disqualification of the respondent No. 5. 

 6. Mr. AKM Mozammel Hoque Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No. 5, who was elected Chairman in the election in question, submitted that the petitioner is not a voter from the area taken out from Nabinagar Upazila and he was aware of the same from the time of the Gazette Notification dated 6.11.89 and neither he nor the voters of the said Union were prejudiced in any manner and the petitioner by giving a go-by to the said delimitation of area participated in the election without raising any objection to the same and the people of the said unions also never raised any objection rather they participated in the election. He further submitted that his client's age was actually 29 years at the time of filing nomination paper on the basis of unassailable documentary evidence and relying upon which the Returning Officer allowed the respondent No. 5 to contest the election accepting his nomination paper without any objection from the other candidates. He further submitted relying on the decision in the case of Farid Miah Vs. Amjad Ali and others reported in 42 DLR (AD) 13 that the question of disqualification cannot be raised before his client's entering office and the petitioner has been challenging election of his client rather than his holding office. He further submitted that one Abdul Latif, Advocate, a candidate in the said election securing next highest number of votes than the elected Chairman, filed Writ Petition No. 650 of 1990 challenging election of his client on the ground of disqualification due to under age and the said petition was rejected on 10.4.90 and thereafter the petitioner, who secured third position in the election, filed this writ petition challenging the election of the respondent No. 5 suppressing the fact of his filing and pendency of the case before the Election Tribunal and this case is not only vexatious but to harass his client and cause loss to him. He further submitted that since name of his client has been published in the official Gazette and the case involves disputed question of fact the writ petition is not maintainable. 

 7. In this case admittedly delimitation of the area of Nabinagar Upazila taking away several villages of two Unions of that Upazila and adding the same with Brahmanbaria Sadar Upazila was made by the Government under section 2A of the Local Government (Upazila Parishad and Upazila Administration Reorganisation) Ordinance, 1982 by notification published in the official Gazette on 6.11.89 by the Deputy Secretary, Ministry of Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives. The petitioner has not impleaded the Government in this writ petition. The petitioner being the sitting Chairman of the Nabinagar Upazila Parishad and an important public figure of the locality at the relevant time must have knowledge of the delimitation of area not only from the time of the proceeding for de-limitation of area but also from the date of publication of the same in the official Gazette and he did not challenge the same so long and participated in the election accepting the delimitation of area of Nabinagar Upazila and after he failed to get himself elected in the said election held on 16.3.90 he filed this case at a belated stage suppressing pendency of the case filed by. him in the Election Tribunal and as such challenge of delimitation of area of Nabinagar Upazila by the petitioner after the election is not maintainable due to the laches of the petitioner and is not also maintainable for not impleading the lithotrity making the delimitation of the area as respondent in this case as the objection to the same cannot be effectively decided in the absence of such authority which is in possession and custody of relevant materials. Whether delimitation of the area of the two Upazilas in question was made in public Interest or not cannot also be decided in the absence of the authority which made the delimitation and which is in possession and custody of the materials in support of their decision to delimitate the area. In our opinion delimitation of area of the Upazilas in question cannot affect the petitioner who is not a resident of any of the villages taken away by the Government from Nabinagar Upazila by the impugned notification. The residents of the villages in question are the only persons who may be said to be affected by the impugned notification and as such the petitioner not being resident of any of the villages in question has no locus standi to challenge the said notification. The learned Advocates of both the parties informed us in course of hearing of the petition that Writ Petition No. 650 of 1990 filed by some of the residents of the villages in question challenging the aforesaid notification is pending for disposal. In our view the decision in that case cannot affect the election in question inasmuch as the election was declared and held long after the delimitation. The respondent No. 5 is not at fault for the delimitation of the area and his election cannot be declared void for no fault of his especially when he is not guilty of any corrupt or illegal practices in holding and conducting the election and the petitioner has not made any such allegation against him in this writ petition.
